focus: 'going to' → /ɡənə/ and 'll /l/ in fast speech · stress on time words · 'present continuous for arrangements' rhythm · weak 'at/on/in' + time
focus_ar: 'going to' → /ɡənə/ و 'll في الكلام السريع، والنبر على كلمات الزمن، وإيقاع الترتيبات، وحروف الوقت الخفيفة
arabic_challenge: B1 juggles three futures; the phonological risk is over-pronouncing 'going to' and stressing the auxiliary instead of the time/plan word. Time expressions ('at six', 'on Monday') also need weak prepositions.

isolation.instructions: Before a verb, 'going to' reduces to /ɡənə/: 'I'm gonna call'. Before a place it stays full: 'going to Cairo'. The main verb takes the stress.
isolation.instructions_ar: قبل الفعل 'going to' → /ɡənə/. قبل المكان تفضل كاملة. النبر على الفعل الرئيسي.

sentence_practice: I'm going to call her tonight.
We're going to meet at six.
They're going to start next week.
daily_drills.record_this: I'm going to call her tonight, and we're going to meet at six. They're going to start the project next week, so I'm going to prepare everything.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I'm going to call'. Does 'going to' become 'gonna', stressed on 'call'?

isolation.instructions: 'Will' contracts to 'll: 'I'll call you back'. Use it for on-the-spot decisions and predictions. One syllable, glued to the pronoun, stress on the verb.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'will' → 'll: 'I'll call'. للقرارات اللحظية والتوقعات. مقطع واحد ملزوق بالضمير، النبر على الفعل.

daily_drills.record_this: Don't worry, I'll help you with that. It'll be fine, I promise. OK, I'll call you later and we'll decide together.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I'll help'. Is it one smooth syllable + stressed verb, not 'I will help'?

isolation.instructions: Future plans put the stress on WHEN: 'I'm meeting her at SIX', 'We're leaving on MONday'. The future marker stays weak; the time word is prominent.
isolation.instructions_ar: خطط المستقبل النبر فيها على الزمن: 'at SIX'، 'on MONday'. علامة المستقبل خفيفة والزمن بارز.

daily_drills.record_this: I'm meeting her at six this evening. We're leaving on Monday morning, and they're arriving next week, probably on Friday.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I'm meeting her at six'. Is 'six' the strongest word?

isolation.instructions: Fixed arrangements use present continuous: 'I'm seeing the doctor tomorrow'. It sounds like now, but the time word makes it future. Auxiliary weak, verb + time stressed.
isolation.instructions_ar: الترتيبات المؤكدة بالمضارع المستمر: 'I'm seeing the doctor tomorrow'. كلمة الزمن تخليها مستقبل.

sentence_practice: We're meeting the team at nine.
daily_drills.record_this: I'm seeing the doctor tomorrow morning. We're meeting the whole team at nine, and she's coming to dinner tonight, so I'm cooking something special.
daily_drills.self_check: Does the arrangement flow with a weak auxiliary and stress on the verb + time word?

target_sounds: choosing the future form by rhythm

isolation.instructions: Contrast all three: 'I'll get it' (instant decision), 'I'm going to study' (intention), 'I'm meeting her at six' (arrangement). Each keeps a weak marker and a stressed content word.
isolation.instructions_ar: قارن الثلاثة: 'I'll get it' (قرار)، 'I'm gonna study' (نية)، 'I'm meeting her at six' (ترتيب). كلها علامة خفيفة + كلمة منبورة.

sentence_practice: That's the phone — I'll get it.
I'm meeting my friends at seven.
daily_drills.record_this: That's the phone — I'll get it. Next year I'm going to study medicine. And tonight I'm meeting my friends at seven, so I'll probably be home late.
daily_drills.self_check: Can you switch between 'I'll', 'gonna' and the continuous, each with a weak marker and stressed content?

challenge_sentences: I'm going to study tonight, but first I'll help you.
We're meeting at six on Monday.
It's going to rain, so I'll take an umbrella.
I'm flying to Cairo next week.
daily_drills.record_this: I'm going to study tonight, but first I'll help you with your homework. We're meeting at six on Monday. Look at those clouds — it's going to rain, so I'll take an umbrella. By the way, I'm flying to Cairo next week.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: 'gonna' before verbs, 'll for decisions, and stress on the time words.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself talking about your plans and arrangements. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تتكلم عن خططك وترتيباتك، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: Next month is going to be very busy. On Monday I'm meeting my new manager at nine, and on Wednesday I'm flying to Cairo for a conference. I'm going to give a presentation there, so this week I'll prepare my slides. I think it'll go well. In the evening I'm having dinner with an old friend — we're meeting at a restaurant near the river. After the trip, I'm going to take a short holiday. I'll probably travel to the coast, and I'm definitely going to relax. Don't worry, I'll send you photos while I'm away.

sounds_to_check.'gonna' (intention): going to be busy, going to give, going to take, going to relax
sounds_to_check.'ll (decisions/predictions): I'll prepare, it'll go well, I'll probably travel, I'll send
sounds_to_check.present continuous (arrangements): I'm meeting, I'm flying, I'm having, we're meeting
sounds_to_check.stress on time words: on MONday at NINE, on WEDNESday, next MONTH
sounds_to_check.full 'going to' before place: flying to Cairo, travel to the coast

scoring_guide.90_100: Three futures used naturally, markers weak, time words stressed. Ready for week 4.
scoring_guide.50_69: Auxiliaries too strong or 'gonna' before places. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, keeping each future marker weak.

for_arabic_speakers: All three futures keep a WEAK marker and stress the content/time word.
'gonna' before a verb; keep 'going to' full before a place.
'll is for on-the-spot decisions and predictions; present continuous is for fixed arrangements.
Stress the WHEN — that is what makes a plan sound like a plan.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
